# Brisbane’s leading luxury real estate agencies and prestige auctioneers

As of October 2026, Brisbane has a strong and increasingly competitive prestige residential market, with established luxury specialists, international luxury-property networks and high-performing auction teams all competing for premium listings.

McGrath’s Spring 2026 prestige report recorded **677 Brisbane residential sales above \$3 million in the year to Q2 2026**, up 16% year on year. Sales above \$5 million increased by 87%, signalling growing importance for agents who can reach high-net-worth buyers and manage complex, high-value negotiations. [www.mcgrath.com.au](https://www.mcgrath.com.au/research/prestige-brisbane-residential-spring-2026-report?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[brisbane.queenslandsothebysrealty.com](https://brisbane.queenslandsothebysrealty.com/team/malcolm-li?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

For a seller of a luxury home, I would distinguish between three things: the agency’s prestige-market credentials, the individual listing agent’s record of achieving premium prices, and the auctioneer’s ability to create competition under the hammer. The strongest choice is not necessarily the agency with the biggest overall sales volume.

## 1\. Leading prestige real estate agencies

![Haesley Cush • Ray White](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/qG7jhlbaw13GS4UvEk3aiQCKaoPq76vKZA7MhwIaKcRQFx8MCfmI_bFOZVgit8uHiLNSFX6i45MCuAlyk-oFKiIUu2LFhzWTWZM3DeSmWeryfA3vQJNlNRaaDX5f90_eKKZuEyGNPMktdtIXBiL76s3qRT-lIHnounpwUQQRcdO2mrFFbKtORV8w11IpW3Aj?purpose=fullsize)

## 1\. Ray White Collective Luxury

(Standout for ultra-luxury auctions)

Best suited to trophy homes, riverfront mansions and properties likely to attract competitive bidding.

**Key names\:** Matt Lancashire and Haesley Cush.

The team has a particularly strong profile in Brisbane’s multimillion-dollar market. Lancashire’s reported results include a \$20.5 million New Farm sale and six luxury homes sold for a combined \$71 million at a single Collective Luxury Auction event. Ray White also reports \$326 million in settled sales for Lancashire during FY2024–25. [www.raywhite.com](https://www.raywhite.com/the-white-report/brisbanes-most-decorated-luxury-agent-marks-20-years-with-ray-white?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## 2\. Adcock Prestige

(Dedicated prestige specialist)

A strong shortlist candidate for blue-chip houses, architectural homes, riverfront properties and premium residences in Brisbane’s inner west.

**Key name\:** Jason Adcock.

Adcock has worked in Brisbane’s prestige market for more than 28 years and established his specialist agency in 2002. His distinctive advantage is combining the listing agent role with auctioneering, giving him direct knowledge of the property and its prospective buyers. ## 2\. Top auctioneers to shortlist

## 3\. My shortlist by property type

### Trophy home or property above \$5 million

**Start with\:** Ray White Collective Luxury, Matt Lancashire and Haesley Cush.

Their documented prestige sales and dedicated luxury auction events make them a logical first interview. [www.raywhite.com](https://www.raywhite.com/the-white-report/brisbanes-most-decorated-luxury-agent-marks-20-years-with-ray-white?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

---

### Architectural, riverfront or inner-west prestige home

**Start with\:** Adcock Prestige and Place Estate Agents.

Compare the individual agent’s recent results for homes with similar architecture, land, outlook and buyer profile.

---

### Luxury home needing international buyer exposure

**Start with\:** Queensland Sotheby’s International Realty.

Ask how many qualified international and interstate buyers are active in your property's price bracket, rather than relying on brand reach alone.

---

### Independent auctioneer for a competitive tender

**Start with\:** Rob Doorey at Apollo Auctions or Jordan Curd at Place.

Request evidence of recent auctions in your property's price range, including bidder numbers and final prices versus pre-auction appraisals.

## 4\. How to identify the genuine top performer

Before signing an agency agreement, ask each shortlisted agent for the following information for the last 12 months\:

- **Comparable settled sales\:** Three to five Brisbane sales in the same price bracket and property category.
- **Price performance\:** Final sale price versus initial appraisal and, where available, reserve.
- **Auction conversion\:** Number of registered bidders, active bidders, properties sold under the hammer, and properties passed in.
- **Buyer depth\:** Evidence of qualified buyers beyond the agent’s existing client or local suburb network.
- **Net vendor outcome\:** Proposed commission, marketing costs, auctioneer fee and any additional charges.
- **Who does the work\:** Whether the named senior agent personally manages inspections, buyer negotiations and auction strategy.

There is no single publicly verified ranking that establishes the best Brisbane luxury agency and best prestige auctioneer across all price brackets. The recommendations above are based on documented prestige-market activity, professional recognition and specialist positioning, not a definitive league table of all agents.

**My overall recommendation\:** Begin with Ray White Collective Luxury and Adcock Prestige for a high-end Brisbane sale, then compare them against Queensland Sotheby’s International Realty or Place depending on the property and target buyer. Interview Haesley Cush and Rob Doorey if you want to assess auctioneering separately from the listing agency.

One question that would materially refine the shortlist: **What type of property and approximate sale price are you considering?** For example, a \$3–5 million inner-city home, a \$5–10 million riverfront residence, or a \$10 million-plus trophy estate.

search_results.title: Hamilton Grove: $1.2b luxury towers break ground in Brisbane
search_results.description: Wentworth Equities has commenced construction on the $1.2 billion Hamilton Grove precinct in Brisbane, marked by an official sod-turning ceremony attended by government representatives. Located in the 304-hectare Northshore Hamilton Priority Development Area, the ambitious project includes three luxury residential towers comprising 292 apartments, a 196-room five-star hotel, 3,000 square meters of retail space, and a vibrant public precinct. Executive Chairman Sameh Ibrahim emphasized the project's historic significance and its aim to redefine apartment living by offering suburban-style space and character in an urban setting. Contractor Mainland Civil, known for its work on other high-profile Brisbane projects such as Queens Wharf and Infinity Tower, is leading construction. The Queensland Government is supporting the broader development of Hamilton Northshore with a $154 million infrastructure investment, aiming to add more than $14 billion to the local economy upon completion. Hamilton Grove has drawn strong buyer interest since its April launch, and future development phases, including the hotel, are already in planning. The project aspires to set a new standard for luxury living in Brisbane with its standout “sky homes” serving as its centerpiece.

search_results.title: Aria's Sanctuary Residences: $519m sold before public launch
search_results.description: Aria Property Group has reported a record-breaking pre-launch success for its Sanctuary Residences project in South Brisbane, achieving $519 million in apartment sales, making it Queensland’s largest apartment launch to date. Remarkably, sales were made without any public advertising, focusing on high-end three and four-bedroom apartments priced from $2.72 million and $4.01 million. Of the 231 apartments available in the first tower, only 86 remain unsold. Designed for buyers seeking spacious, luxurious homes without downsizing, the project has attracted strong interest. The development at 164-190 Melbourne Street includes restoration of two heritage buildings and features expansive amenities such as a wellness club, rooftop bar, and 2.9-meter ceilings. It is part of a larger master-planned precinct with public parks, laneways, and retail spaces. The first tower is set to complete by mid-to-late 2029, aligning with Brisbane's preparation for the 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games. This overwhelming response reflects growing demand for high-quality apartment living in Brisbane. The remaining units will be publicly released on October 19, with potential price increases expected.

search_results.title: Graya breaks ground on Brisbane's most expensive house in New Farm
search_results.description: Celebrity developers Graya have commenced construction on a lavish mansion dubbed “Ivory,” on an exclusive riverfront block in New Farm, Brisbane, purchased by Chemist Warehouse boss Jeff Wasley and his wife Tanya for a record-breaking $25 million in 2025. Designed and built by Graya over 11 months, the home is expected to be worth between $40-$50 million upon completion. The 688 sqm site was previously owned by Graya co-founder Rob Gray and originally intended as his personal residence before it was sold for a $16.5 million profit. Ivory features a five-storey design including high-end amenities such as a luxury car showroom with river views, resort-style pools, rooftop entertainment areas, a wellness center, state-of-the-art golf simulator, and a master suite with 10-meter wardrobes. The house boasts a sleek, neutral finish with white, curved terraces and mushroom-style pillars. Located between New Farm Park and the Story Bridge, the property offers panoramic views of Brisbane’s skyline. This milestone build reflects Graya’s continued influence in Brisbane's luxury real estate market. The Wasleys had previously acquired another Graya-built home in Hamilton for $12.5 million.

search_results.title: Villa Alcyone: Award-winning Elanora mansion eyes suburb record
search_results.description: Villa Alcyone, a Mediterranean-style mansion situated on a steep 890 sqm block at 6 Bicton Ct in Elanora, has entered the market with expectations to surpass the suburb's sales record by millions. Designed by Jayson Pate and built by Resolve Constructions, the award-winning home reflects a growing trend of luxury builders tackling challenging vertical sites. The property garnered multiple accolades at the 2026 HIA Gold Coast and Northern Rivers Awards and a Master Builders Queensland award. The four-bedroom, four-bathroom home spans 579 sqm and features high-end finishes such as Italian marble, dramatic archways, and a Sukabumi stone pool, all inspired by European influences during the owners' travels. Interior design was led by co-owner Helen Foukkare. Positioned to maximize ocean views and offering access to popular nearby beaches like Currumbin and Palm Beach, the mansion is drawing interest from high-end buyers typically focused on more traditionally prestigious areas. Although quarterly data shows a slight dip in Elanora home prices, the suburb's annual values rose 14.7 percent, reflecting its evolving luxury market appeal. The Foukkares are already planning another unique luxury build in the Gold Coast region.

search_results.title: Inside Katanga: Hamilton's grand 1884 riverfront estate for sale
search_results.description: Katanga, a prestigious 1884 riverfront estate in Hamilton, Brisbane, is now on the market after an extensive transformation blending historical charm with modern luxury. Located at 25 Langside Road on a 1113 m² plot, the home has been thoughtfully redesigned by Twohill & James, maintaining its original heritage while introducing contemporary, lift-connected living across three levels. Current owners Sam and Brad Hopper, who previously owned a prominent Sunshine Beach property, sought to honor the home's history through elegant updates, including Calacatta Viola marble and travertine finishes. The residence features five ensuite bedrooms, including a luxurious parents' retreat, a self-contained guest wing, and numerous leisure amenities such as a gym, sauna, cinema, alfresco terrace, wet-edge pool, and heated spa. The impressive kitchen and entertaining areas integrate seamlessly with modern family functionality, while features such as a 10-car garage, dual EV chargers, and private office further enhance its appeal. With its sweeping river views and seamless blend of old and new, Katanga is a rare Brisbane gem now ready for new owners.

search_results.title: Ray White TMG Luxury launches amid Gold Coast market downturn
search_results.description: Ray White TMG Luxury has launched amid a downturn in the Gold Coast property market, marked by four interest rate hikes, Middle East conflict, and changes to federal property tax policies. Ray White chief economist Nerida Conisbee remarked on the market’s uncertainty, though noting it is currently easier to transact. The launch featured a premium Broadbeach Waters property at 29 Namatjira Court with 95m of river frontage, 533 sq m of luxury living space, and high-end amenities such as a cocktail lounge and riverside pool. Despite a 3% decline in overall Gold Coast property values over the past year, the luxury segment in Broadbeach Waters remains resilient, mirroring stabilizing trends in Sydney’s Eastern suburbs and Melbourne’s South Yarra and Toorak. The event also marked the official unveiling of Ray White TMG Luxury, a new prestige-focused division led by CEO Matt Micallef. Micallef emphasized the division’s goal to provide a specialist approach for high-end buyers and sellers, asserting the Gold Coast's legitimacy as a top-tier luxury market. The luxury brand aims to respond to growing demand with dedicated, high-caliber service.

# Brisbane’s leading luxury real estate agencies and prestige auctioneers

As of October 2026, Brisbane has a strong and increasingly competitive prestige residential market, with established luxury specialists, international luxury-property networks and high-performing auction teams all competing for premium listings.

McGrath’s Spring 2026 prestige report recorded **677 Brisbane residential sales above \$3 million in the year to Q2 2026**, up 16% year on year. Sales above \$5 million increased by 87%, signalling growing importance for agents who can reach high-net-worth buyers and manage complex, high-value negotiations. [www.mcgrath.com.au](https://www.mcgrath.com.au/research/prestige-brisbane-residential-spring-2026-report?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[brisbane.queenslandsothebysrealty.com](https://brisbane.queenslandsothebysrealty.com/team/malcolm-li?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

For a seller of a luxury home, I would distinguish between three things: the agency’s prestige-market credentials, the individual listing agent’s record of achieving premium prices, and the auctioneer’s ability to create competition under the hammer. The strongest choice is not necessarily the agency with the biggest overall sales volume.

## 1\. Leading prestige real estate agencies

![Haesley Cush • Ray White](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/qG7jhlbaw13GS4UvEk3aiQCKaoPq76vKZA7MhwIaKcRQFx8MCfmI_bFOZVgit8uHiLNSFX6i45MCuAlyk-oFKiIUu2LFhzWTWZM3DeSmWeryfA3vQJNlNRaaDX5f90_eKKZuEyGNPMktdtIXBiL76s3qRT-lIHnounpwUQQRcdO2mrFFbKtORV8w11IpW3Aj?purpose=fullsize)

## 1\. Ray White Collective Luxury

(Standout for ultra-luxury auctions)

Best suited to trophy homes, riverfront mansions and properties likely to attract competitive bidding.

**Key names\:** Matt Lancashire and Haesley Cush.

The team has a particularly strong profile in Brisbane’s multimillion-dollar market. Lancashire’s reported results include a \$20.5 million New Farm sale and six luxury homes sold for a combined \$71 million at a single Collective Luxury Auction event. Ray White also reports \$326 million in settled sales for Lancashire during FY2024–25. [www.raywhite.com](https://www.raywhite.com/the-white-report/brisbanes-most-decorated-luxury-agent-marks-20-years-with-ray-white?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## 3\. My shortlist by property type

### Trophy home or property above \$5 million

**Start with\:** Ray White Collective Luxury, Matt Lancashire and Haesley Cush.

Their documented prestige sales and dedicated luxury auction events make them a logical first interview. [www.raywhite.com](https://www.raywhite.com/the-white-report/brisbanes-most-decorated-luxury-agent-marks-20-years-with-ray-white?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

---

### Architectural, riverfront or inner-west prestige home

**Start with\:** Adcock Prestige and Place Estate Agents.

Compare the individual agent’s recent results for homes with similar architecture, land, outlook and buyer profile.

---

### Luxury home needing international buyer exposure

**Start with\:** Queensland Sotheby’s International Realty.

Ask how many qualified international and interstate buyers are active in your property's price bracket, rather than relying on brand reach alone.

---

### Independent auctioneer for a competitive tender

**Start with\:** Rob Doorey at Apollo Auctions or Jordan Curd at Place.

Request evidence of recent auctions in your property's price range, including bidder numbers and final prices versus pre-auction appraisals.

## 4\. How to identify the genuine top performer

Before signing an agency agreement, ask each shortlisted agent for the following information for the last 12 months\:

- **Comparable settled sales\:** Three to five Brisbane sales in the same price bracket and property category.
- **Price performance\:** Final sale price versus initial appraisal and, where available, reserve.
- **Auction conversion\:** Number of registered bidders, active bidders, properties sold under the hammer, and properties passed in.
- **Buyer depth\:** Evidence of qualified buyers beyond the agent’s existing client or local suburb network.
- **Net vendor outcome\:** Proposed commission, marketing costs, auctioneer fee and any additional charges.
- **Who does the work\:** Whether the named senior agent personally manages inspections, buyer negotiations and auction strategy.

There is no single publicly verified ranking that establishes the best Brisbane luxury agency and best prestige auctioneer across all price brackets. The recommendations above are based on documented prestige-market activity, professional recognition and specialist positioning, not a definitive league table of all agents.

**My overall recommendation\:** Begin with Ray White Collective Luxury and Adcock Prestige for a high-end Brisbane sale, then compare them against Queensland Sotheby’s International Realty or Place depending on the property and target buyer. Interview Haesley Cush and Rob Doorey if you want to assess auctioneering separately from the listing agency.

One question that would materially refine the shortlist: **What type of property and approximate sale price are you considering?** For example, a \$3–5 million inner-city home, a \$5–10 million riverfront residence, or a \$10 million-plus trophy estate.
